item.title: Padikkal or Sudharsan? Manjrekar makes No. 3 call: 'He looks formidable'
item.description: On the first day in Galle, Devdutt Padikkal shone brightly, scoring an unbeaten 131 runs. His technique against Sri Lanka's spinners garnered high praise from Sanjay Manjrekar, who noted Padikkal's impressive back-foot play and attacking style. This stellar performance strengthens his candidacy for the number three batting slot and marks a notable milestone in the young Indian cricketer's career.

item.title: MacKenzie Scott helped abolish $40B in medical debt; how mechanics work
item.description: MacKenzie Scott has pioneered large-scale medical debt relief through significant donations. Her gifts enabled the abolition of over forty billion dollars in medical debt. This initiative has provided relief to millions of families across all fifty states. Other billionaires have been inspired by this effective philanthropic model. However, policy reform remains stalled, highlighting the model's limitations.

item.title: Indian-American CEO who sacked 900 over Zoom gets fired himself
item.description: Indian-American entrepreneur Vishal Garg has been ousted as Better Home & Finance CEO. The company cited concerns about his judgment and credibility after significant losses. Garg's removal follows his controversial 2021 mass layoff of 900 employees. He is now seeking to regain his position and is offering to work for one dollar annually. Better's market value has significantly decreased since its pandemic-era peak.
item.dc:creator: CHIDANAND RAJGHATTA

item.title: Zohran Mamdani’s ‘common sense regulation’ may push Amazon to move NYC deliveries
item.description: In New York City, Mayor Zohran Mamdani is advocating for a bill that mandates direct employment for delivery drivers. Amazon has raised concerns that this legislation could push its delivery services outside the city limits. Critics point out that the bill might lead to a sharp increase in delivery costs for residents. Additionally, opponents warn that the legislation could jeopardize countless delivery jobs and adversely affect local businesses.

item.title: OpenAI's S7 data centre drops plan to cool it with recycled water after permit snags
item.description: OpenAI has decided to discontinue its plans for implementing recycled water cooling at its Sydney data center due to regulatory hurdles that hindered the necessary pipeline's construction. Consequently, the facility will adopt a more energy-intensive closed-loop liquid cooling system. This transition comes amidst Sydney's growing demand for data centers. Notably, the S7 data center is projected to generate thousands of jobs during its construction phase.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: For 12 remote villages near China border, power is finally in sight
item.description: Remote villages in Uttarakhand's Johar Valley will soon receive grid electricity for the first time. This significant development will benefit approximately 180 seasonal residents and ITBP personnel stationed there. The electrification project, costing Rs 21 crore, spans sixty-one kilometers and includes twelve villages. Power lines have been laid up to Rasgadi, with Bugdiyar also slated for electrification shortly.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes, Brittany Mahomes' $5 million act builds lasting Texas legacy
item.description: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' recent $5 million donation to Texas Tech marks a transformative moment for the university's football facilities. This substantial amount amplifies the fundraising efforts and ensures naming rights for prominent sections of the new complex. With Patrick's rich history at Texas Tech, their generosity underscores a lasting commitment to elevating the school's athletic programs to new heights.

item.title: Khabib Nurmagomedov sends special message to Islam Makhachev ahead of UFC 330
item.description: Khabib Nurmagomedov has praised Islam Makhachev's dedicated journey ahead of his significant welterweight title defense. Makhachev will face Ian Machado Garry at UFC 330 in Philadelphia this Saturday. While many expect Makhachev to win, Nurmagomedov respects Garry's fighting capabilities. Makhachev aims to extend his impressive winning streak to seventeen victories. Garry, an underdog, seeks to build his own significant fighting legacy.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: 'I sincerely apologise': BCI chief to law students after row over NALSAR diktat
item.description: In a heartfelt gesture, Bar Council of India chairman Manan Kumar Mishra issued an apology to law students, expressing regret if his statements or a letter had caused any distress. This move came after a significant uproar involving a guest invitation for NALSAR University’s convocation. Initially, the Council had intervened but later retracted its guidance, with the Supreme Court subsequently questioning the Bar Council’s role in the matter.
item.dc:creator: MANVI VYAS

item.title: Trump eyes millions from personal political funds for GOP amid midterm fears: Report
item.description: President Trump has reportedly greenlit substantial funding from his PAC to bolster Republican candidates ahead of the upcoming midterms. He is ramping up his campaign appearances, aiming to energize his dedicated base amid challenges to maintain Congressional control. This strategic push also seeks to address growing unease surrounding issues like the Iran conflict and rising gas prices.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: E20 mileage row: Govt says fuel alone can't be blamed; cites driving & maintenance
item.description: The government clarifies that the introduction of E20 petrol does not hinder vehicle mileage, emphasizing that actual fuel efficiency hinges on how drivers operate their vehicles and maintain them. Comprehensive assessments confirmed that E20 fuel is both durable and compatible with engines. Additionally, no significant contamination issues were discovered in E20 petrol samples by oil companies, instilling confidence in its performance and vehicle compatibility.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: FSSAI revokes liquor prohibition: Regulator withdraws 11-brand ban in Tamil Nadu
item.description: While FSSAI's U-turn raised eyebrows, officials said that the company had appealed against the prohibition order promising compliance, after which the prohibition was revoked and instead an improvement notice was issued.

item.title: Flashback: What happened when India last hosted BWF World Championships
item.description: New Delhi is set to welcome the prestigious 2026 Badminton World Championships after a long hiatus of seventeen years. The last event in 2009 in Hyderabad witnessed China's commanding presence, highlighted by Lin Dan's monumental victory. With the stakes higher than ever, India prepares to write a new chapter in this thrilling sport, reflecting the dramatic shifts in international badminton.

item.title: 'I now know I was wrong': Hikaru on chaotic EWC match against Firouzja
item.description: Hikaru Nakamura finished third at the 2026 Esports World Cup after Alireza Firouzja forfeited their match following technical issues and multiple disconnections. Initially blaming chess.com, Nakamura later learned the problems were caused by the EWC. He apologised for his comments, admitted he jumped to conclusions, and earned $145,000 plus valuable Club Championship points for Falcons Esports.

item.title: Cauvery row: Water released from KRS? BJP claim puts Karnataka govt on spot
item.description: The release of Cauvery water from Karnataka to Tamil Nadu has sparked debates, particularly after a BJP claim that water was released late at night from KRS. This event holds substantial implications for farmers and political groups in Mandya. Karnataka is set to appeal the water release directive in the Supreme Court, with officials proposing that a limited release could indicate compliance as they navigate the legal battle.
item.dc:creator: MANUAIYAPPA KANATHANDA

item.title: KL Rahul injury scare? India coach gives big update after batter retires hurt
item.description: KL Rahul is “fine now” after retiring hurt with cramps during India’s Test against Sri Lanka, batting coach Sitanshu Kotak said. Rahul scored 77 off 162 balls and shared a 150-run stand with Devdutt Padikkal. Padikkal hit an unbeaten 131 on his Test comeback, while India finished day one strongly at 288 for two.

item.title: ‘The way he has prepared’: India coach explains key to Padikkal’s maiden century
item.description: Devdutt Padikkal scored an unbeaten 131 on his maiden international century. His improved back-foot game was credited by batting coach Sitanshu Kotak. Padikkal adapted well to Sri Lanka's spin-heavy bowling attack. KL Rahul also contributed significantly before retiring hurt from the match. Sri Lanka's coach praised both Indian batters for their performances.

item.title: 80 years on, still enemy No. 1: What Indians and Pakistanis think of each other
item.description: A recent survey by Pew highlights that Indians and Pakistanis regard each other as their principal geopolitical adversaries. Unfavorable opinions dominate across the border, with India marking Pakistan as the major threat while Pakistan responds in kind. There is a notable distrust regarding the other’s dedication to peaceful relations, amplified by contrasting global alliances influencing each country’s strategic outlook.

item.title: Devdutt Padikkal joins Virat Kohli in elite club after historic ton vs Sri Lanka
item.description: On Independence Day, Devdutt Padikkal made history by becoming the second Indian and the first to score an international Test century on August 15. His remarkable innings had him finishing Day 1 undefeated at 131 runs, solidifying his place at number three in the batting order. This impressive achievement marks the end of India's long wait for a Test century from that position.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: Midnight wasn't the end: What happened in first few hours of Independent India
item.description: India's liberation from British rule was celebrated at midnight on August 15, 1947, as Jawaharlal Nehru captivated everyone with his famed 'Tryst with Destiny' speech. Following this historic moment, the newly formed government not only celebrated freedom but also faced daunting challenges related to governance and nation-building, with Lord Mountbatten taking charge as the first Governor-General during a time marked by the chaos of Partition.

item.title: A ton of class! Devdutt Padikkal makes the long wait count
item.description: Devdutt Padikkal last played a Test for India during the 2024 Border-Gavaskar Trophy in Australia. After waiting 632 days, the left-hander seized his opportunity. Karnataka captaincy, role clarity and work on his game against spin reaped rewards as he put India in a dominant position with his maiden ton and a 150-run stand with his statemate and coffee partner KL Rahul on the opening day of the first Test in Galle.
item.dc:creator: SAHIL MALHOTRA

item.title: US housing squeeze: Over 50% of families burdened by rent; here's how much tenants pay
item.description: Over 50% of renter families in America struggle with exorbitant housing costs, largely due to a chronic shortage of available homes that maintains high rental prices nationwide. Lower-income families bear the brunt of these escalating expenses, as zoning limitations and regulatory challenges obstruct new construction initiatives. Experts anticipate that upcoming housing legislation could eventually influence market pricing dynamics.
item.dc:creator: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK

item.title: BWF World C'ships: Beyond smashes, drops, the conditions could decide the winner
item.description: At the BWF World Championships in Delhi, starting from Monday, the biggest challenge may not come from the opponent across the net. Drafts, heat and humidity could prove decisive as the world's best adapt to tricky conditions.
item.dc:creator: TANUJ LAKHINA

item.title: Gurgaon’s annual road-repair cycle: 10 ways to fix the problem, not just the potholes
item.description: Gurgaon consistently suffers from road damage and waterlogging following significant monsoon rains. This ongoing issue highlights persistent drainage and construction flaws that have yet to be resolved. Despite ongoing investments in repairs, the city fails to tackle the fundamental causes of its infrastructure issues. Roads function within an interdependent network where adequate drainage is essential.
item.dc:creator: BIJU MATHEW AND AKANKSHA GUPTA

item.title: Shooting at US University leaves 5 injured, 1 critical; campus lockdown lifted
item.description: Virginia State University experienced a lockdown early Saturday following a shooting incident. Multiple suspects were involved, and several individuals sustained injuries near the Quad Annexes. Campus police confirmed that victims were transported to local hospitals for necessary medical treatment. Both university and county police are actively investigating the circumstances surrounding the shooting event. Authorities have not yet released specific details regarding the suspects or the injured parties.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: 'Remove bulletproof glass or I wont speak': PM told officers ahead of 2014 I-Day
item.description: Former defence secretary RK Mathur has recalled how Prime Minister Narendra Modi insisted on removing the bulletproof glass barrier from the Red Fort before delivering his first Independence Day address as Prime Minister in 2014. Speaking about the episode, Mathur said he and the then Director of the Intelligence Bureau (IB) had briefed Modi about the security arrangements ahead of August 15.
item.dc:creator: TOI NEWS DESK

item.title: Harmanpreet Singh's brace powers India to 3-1 win over Wales in World Cup opener
item.description: India began their FIH Hockey World Cup campaign with a strong 3-1 victory over Wales. Captain Harmanpreet Singh scored two goals, leading the team's dominant performance. Sanjay opened the scoring for India in the eighth minute of the match. Wales managed to pull one goal back late in the game. India secured three points from their opening Pool D fixture.

item.title: Steve Smith creates history, equals Joe Root's world record in 124 Tests
item.description: In a thrilling display of skill, Steve Smith has matched Joe Root's remarkable world record for non-wicketkeeper Test catches, reaching 218 during the first Test against Bangladesh. Smith's achievement, accomplished with three catches at second slip, showcases his talent as he reaches this landmark in far fewer matches than Root. This puts Smith at the pinnacle of the all-time catching leaderboard.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: USS Abraham Lincoln to return home amid rising scrutiny over sailor welfare
item.description: After an extended deployment, the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier is making its way home. While Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao minimized reports of sailor difficulties and supply deficiencies, the Navy contends that allegations regarding a mental health crisis aboard are overstated. This lengthy deployment highlights the pressures faced by the US Navy's carrier fleet, with the USS George Washington set to take over its operations in the Middle East.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Chandigarh police use tear gas to stop Qaumi Insaaf morcha march towards guv's house
item.description: Amid escalating tensions, law enforcement deployed tear gas and water cannons to scatter protesters intending to reach the Governor's residence. Clad in solidarity, attendees attempted to breach police barricades while advocating for the release of Sikh prisoners. The march, led by the Qaumi Insaaf Morcha, found support from multiple Sikh organizations, showcasing the strength of their campaign for the freedom of 'Bandi Singhs' at the Chandigarh-Mohali borders.
item.dc:creator: PAWAN TIWARI
